briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Green Shoots Amid the Grind: Michigan Chases Tax Relief as National Cannabis & Psychedelics Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan operators are pushing toward real relief on the 24% wholesale tax — via a September trial, a fresh tax-pyramiding lawsuit, and a competitive governor's race where both major-party nominees now back a rollback. Nationally, the DEA's rescheduling hearing has reached closing arguments, the FDA is opening the door to psychedelic therapeutics, and major operators are pursuing aggressive M&A, signaling real growth capital is back in the game.

local.text: Fields Cannary's hospitality-driven dispensary-restaurant buildout in Muskegon is moving forward, proof that ambitious, experience-first cannabis retail concepts are still finding runway in Michigan despite market headwinds.

Jars Cannabis — a 54-store chain spanning Michigan, Arizona and Colorado — reached a resolution with Madison Heights officials to remove a surveillance camera tied to a years-old licensing dispute, clearing the way for smoother day-to-day operations at the location.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a 'Freedom Agenda' plank pledging to cut Michigan's cannabis excise tax from 10% to 5% and roll back the wholesale tax, arguing it 'drives up prices' and cedes ground to illicit sellers — giving operators a concrete policy target to organize around ahead of November.

The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's original wholesale-tax challenge is now headed to trial this month, while a second suit targets 'tax pyramiding' that pushes the effective consumer tax rate above the constitutional 6% cap — two live legal paths that could still unwind the levy.

State Treasury is giving businesses breathing room in this first year of the tax, waiving penalties and interest on the first three 2026 quarters for any business that pays at least 75% of what it owes — a practical cushion while the legal fight plays out.

national.text: DEA's marijuana rescheduling hearing reached its closing-argument stage in late August, moving the Schedule III process closer to a final administrative recommendation after months of hearings — the clearest sign yet that federal reclassification is entering its final stretch.

The FDA finalized its first clinical-trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and set a September 14 public hearing on therapeutic psychedelics, while Compass Pathways is now targeting a Q4 2026 NDA submission for its psilocybin therapy COMP360 after receiving a National Priority Voucher that compresses FDA review to roughly one to two months.

Curaleaf pressed its $272 million hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis today, issuing a fact sheet rebutting Aurora's board after the board unanimously urged shareholders to reject the offer — a consolidation fight that underscores how much capital is chasing global cannabis scale right now.

Cresco Labs closed a $50 million acquisition of nine Pennsylvania medical marijuana dispensaries, the latest multistate operator move to lock in market share ahead of anticipated federal policy shifts.

The House is expected to take up Senate-passed legislation this week delaying the federal recriminalization of hemp-derived THC products, buying lawmakers time to craft regulation instead of an outright ban — a reprieve for the broader hemp and cannabinoid supply chain.
